title: Merrily We Roll Along
events_chronological: On a New York rooftop the composer Franklin Shepard, the lyricist Charley Kringas and the writer Mary Flynn watch a satellite cross the sky and promise each other they will make something that matters.
Frank and Charley write songs together in a cramped apartment while Mary starts a novel.
Frank marries Beth, and the three friends scrape a living out of revue material.
Their revue opens off Broadway, and the producer's wife Gussie Carnegie takes a close interest in Frank.
Frank and Beth's son is born.
Frank and Gussie begin an affair at a party in Gussie's house, and Beth watches it happen.
Beth divorces Frank and is given custody of their son in court.
Frank and Charley's musical becomes a hit, and Frank starts producing shows instead of writing them.
During a live television interview Charley sings a public denunciation of Frank, and the partnership ends on air.
Mary's novel is dismissed by the critics and she begins drinking in earnest.
Frank marries Gussie and moves to California to produce films.
At a party at Frank's house on the coast, Gussie throws iodine into the face of Frank's young lover.
A drunk Mary tells Frank at the same party that he has thrown away everything he had, and walks out on him for good.
syuzhet_notes: The nine scenes run backwards from 1976 to 1957, with a transition between each pair that literally reverses the action. Told-order bullets 1-3 are the ruin and bullets 12-13 the rooftop where it started.
fabula_notes: Every scene carries a year, so the chronology is exact. The first two told-order bullets belong to one continuous party and therefore play in order, as do the last two.
